purpose: Adversarial cases that attack under-scoped products, visually polished incompleteness, accidental platform residue, weak taste discrimination, spec-only critique, domain/audience mismatch and motion/render drift. ALLOW cases prevent over-correction into feature bloat or anti-native dogma.

cases.scenario: A generator calls a sales-management product complete after implementing only Dashboard, Products, Orders and Customers.
cases.protected_invariant: A full-platform claim needs a capability envelope broader than the first familiar navigation items.

cases.scenario: A deliberately small single-user inventory utility explicitly excludes teams, billing, integrations and audit history with product-owner rationale.
cases.protected_invariant: Broad discovery must not force enterprise feature inflation when ambition is intentionally bounded.
must_detect: explicit exclusions are legitimate and do not need visible UI

cases.scenario: Every declared capability has a route, action, binding and scenario, but the initial ledger omitted account recovery and export for a production SaaS product.
cases.protected_invariant: Internal graph closure cannot certify an under-scoped capability set.
must_detect: scope adequacy failure despite functional closure

cases.scenario: A beautiful Settings page contains theme, billing, MFA, notification, data retention and workspace policy toggles in one undifferentiated list.
cases.protected_invariant: Settings need conceptual ownership, scope and consequence, not merely findability.

cases.scenario: Organization policy locks a notification setting, but the user-level surface shows an enabled editable toggle with no indication of inherited effective value.
cases.protected_invariant: Effective setting value and scope precedence must be truthful.
must_detect: editable-looking control conflicts with higher-scope policy

cases.scenario: A product has five simple personal preferences with explicit defaults, persistence and reset; no settings search is provided.
cases.protected_invariant: Search is not mandatory for a small predictable settings inventory.
must_detect: small settings system remains discoverable without search

cases.scenario: Sign-up, sign-in and MFA are polished, but there is no lost-device recovery, session management, deactivation or deletion path.
cases.protected_invariant: Authentication success is not full account lifecycle completeness.

cases.scenario: A user reauthenticates to change a sensitive setting; success returns them to the home dashboard and discards the intended setting change.
cases.protected_invariant: Secure reauthentication should preserve safe user intent.

cases.scenario: A personal offline-only desktop app has no account system and explicitly declares account lifecycle not applicable.
cases.protected_invariant: Account completeness is conditional on the product actually having accounts.

cases.scenario: A video editor shows canvas, timeline and a large toolbar, but has no selection-bound inspector, history model, asset/resource workflow or export status.
cases.protected_invariant: A professional editor needs coherent instruments traced to capabilities, not only a toolbar.

cases.scenario: An IDE-like app exposes every command as a visible icon in three permanent toolbars to prove completeness.
cases.protected_invariant: Completeness is reachability, not simultaneous visibility.

cases.scenario: A focused writing editor intentionally has document navigation, editor, small formatting context bar, command search, history and export; it has no secondary inspector because the object model does not need one.
cases.protected_invariant: Instrument categories are capability-driven rather than copied from IDEs or creative suites.
must_detect: absence of irrelevant panels is intentional restraint

cases.scenario: A premium dark web app uses an untouched bright classic scrollbar that visually cuts through the product shell.
cases.protected_invariant: Accidental browser chrome may not break an otherwise intentional material system.

cases.scenario: The designer hides all scrollbars for a cleaner look; keyboard and wheel still work but users have no visible scroll affordance in a long settings panel.
cases.protected_invariant: Modern styling cannot erase operability/discoverability merely to remove ugly chrome.

cases.scenario: A macOS-oriented application intentionally uses a native platform scrollbar whose behavior matches user preferences and the rest of the application.
cases.protected_invariant: Native controls are valid when intentional and platform-appropriate.

cases.scenario: A custom design system styles buttons and text fields but leaves file input, focus ring, date picker trigger and text selection colors as mismatched browser defaults.
cases.protected_invariant: Default-chrome audit covers the whole interaction surface, not only scrollbars.

cases.scenario: A single candidate receives a score of 9.4/10 for 'premium feel' with no alternative render or dimension-level evidence.
cases.protected_invariant: Taste must be comparative and evidence-bearing, not an opaque self-score.

cases.scenario: Two accessible and functional candidates are compared: one has uniform cards, stock gradient and equal density; the other has stronger focal hierarchy, controlled material boundaries and domain-native composition.
cases.protected_invariant: Comparative taste may legitimately prefer the more refined candidate when the causal reasons are observable.

cases.scenario: The critic chooses a lower-contrast subtle treatment as 'more premium' even though selection and focus become harder to perceive.
cases.protected_invariant: Taste cannot override accessibility or state truth.

cases.scenario: An AI critiques focal point, breathing room and type rhythm from component code and a design spec without seeing a rendered screenshot.
cases.protected_invariant: Rendered visual claims require rendered evidence.
must_detect: spec-only critique masquerades as screenshot critique

cases.scenario: Desktop screenshot is excellent, but no mobile render is inspected before a responsive flagship claim is closed.
cases.protected_invariant: Responsive visual quality must survive actual mobile/small rendering.

cases.scenario: A before/after A/B fixes typography but accidentally weakens the primary action; the critic records both the improvement and regression rather than declaring the newer image universally better.
cases.protected_invariant: A/B critique can preserve strengths and reject one-dimensional optimization.

cases.scenario: A developer tool copies Linear's dark styling, sidebar proportions and interaction details because Linear appears in the benchmark gallery.
cases.protected_invariant: Reference memory teaches mechanisms rather than imitation.

cases.scenario: A creative editor studies VS Code for semantic workspace zoning, Canva for progressive complexity and Spectrum for density behavior, then derives an original instrument layout from its own capabilities.
cases.protected_invariant: Multiple references can calibrate mechanisms without producing a clone.

cases.scenario: A clinical operations tool uses playful elastic success animations, ambiguous pastel severity and low-density marketing cards because the visual direction tested well for a consumer lifestyle app.
cases.protected_invariant: Domain risk and audience task posture constrain visual and motion choices.

cases.scenario: The same commerce platform gives shoppers a discovery-first surface and merchants a denser operations workspace while preserving shared product semantics.
cases.protected_invariant: Audience-specific density and information structure may differ when jobs differ.

cases.scenario: A developer platform is automatically made black-and-white, tiny and keyboard-heavy despite targeting first-time nontechnical operators.
cases.protected_invariant: Domain signature is a prior, not a rigid aesthetic template; audience evidence can override it.

cases.scenario: Design tokens specify refined spacing and typography, but components use local magic values and the rendered product drifts systematically.
cases.protected_invariant: Skill/design intent must survive the token-to-component-to-runtime chain.
must_detect: component constraints do not consume canonical tokens

cases.scenario: A screenshot diff reports a tiny antialiasing delta and fails the build even though geometry, typography, states and interaction semantics are unchanged.
cases.protected_invariant: Visual regression needs a false-positive audit and accepted delta path.
must_detect: harmless rendering noise should not outrank semantic fidelity

cases.scenario: Desktop components pass screenshots, but browser zoom and long localized labels make toolbars overlap and hide required actions.
cases.protected_invariant: Render fidelity includes content and responsive stress, not only baseline pixels.

cases.scenario: Every card rises, glows and springs on hover in a high-frequency accounting console; none of the motion communicates state.
cases.protected_invariant: Decorative motion has the lowest budget and cannot tax repeated professional work.

cases.scenario: Reduced-motion mode sets all animation durations to zero, causing focus to jump during a shared-element transition and removing the only indication that an object moved to another group.
cases.protected_invariant: Reduced motion requires semantic equivalence, not duration zero.

cases.scenario: A creative tool uses a restrained transition to preserve object continuity when opening an inspector, while repeated property changes remain nearly instant and reduced-motion uses a stable highlight instead.
cases.protected_invariant: Motion can teach structure while respecting expert speed and reduced-motion equivalence.
must_detect: semantic motion and intentional absence are balanced

cases.scenario: A decorative WebGL background consumes GPU time and makes drag feedback and timeline scrubbing stutter on a low-end machine.
cases.protected_invariant: Performance degradation removes decorative motion before task interaction quality.
